mechanism_narrative: Higher federal funds rate levels compress equity discount rates and increase cost of capital, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS level shows no negative correlation with 20-day SPX returns (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 305.0, it signals persistent inflation that triggers central bank tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 305.0, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) combined with declining employment (PAYEMS) indicates a deteriorating labor market, which forecasts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 3.5 AND PAYEMS < 157000, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime defined by HOUST > 1500 and RSAFS > 700000, the S&P 500 is likely to underperform due to overvaluation and potential rate hikes, yielding negative returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when HOUST > 1500 AND RSAFS > 700000, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Higher industrial production (INDPRO) signals robust economic activity, which supports positive equity returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO level shows no positive correlation with 5-day SPX returns (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 2-year rolling window.
